ai.title: Revert PostHog analytics host to direct endpoint
ai.summary: Reverts `npm-app/src/utils/analytics.ts` to use `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST_URL` for the PostHog client host, bypassing the internal proxy path. This restores direct analytics ingestion, undoing the previous refactor that routed events through `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL}/ingest`.

eli5.text: Analytics events from the app are now sent directly to PostHog's own servers instead of being routed through an internal proxy path. If you looked at the network traffic, you'd see events going straight to the analytics provider rather than passing through the application's own ingestion endpoint. This restores direct analytics collection for everyone using the app.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.298
ai.summary: Version field in `npm-app/package.json` updated from 1.0.297 to 1.0.298. Internal maintenance release. Affects `codebuff` package metadata.

eli5.text: Your AI coding assistant got a small version-number bump, which is the packaging step that bundles together a set of fixes shipped over the past couple of weeks. If you update, you get a smarter entity detector for special characters, automated daily evaluations to keep code quality steady, and a new cost-tracking command. Nothing will visibly break for you; this is routine behind-the-scenes housekeeping that keeps the tool installed and up to date.

ai.title: Remove gemini-api and gemini-vertex-api modules
ai.summary: Deleted `backend/src/llm-apis/gemini-api.ts` and `backend/src/llm-apis/gemini-vertex-api.ts` to consolidate Gemini handling into the Vercel AI SDK. Updated `backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts` to remove `GeminiMessage` type dependencies and deprecated message role handling (developer, function, image_url, input_audio, refusal). Adjusted `backend/src/admin/relabelRuns.ts` to use standard `Message` types instead of `GeminiMessage`.

eli5.text: The software stopped maintaining two separate Gemini connection methods and now uses a single, shared path for all Gemini conversations. If you relied on internal admin tools to re-label conversations, you may need to restart the process because the message-handling step changed how messages are prepared. The old Gemini-specific connection files were deleted, and the system was simplified to remove outdated message types that nothing actively used anymore.

ai.title: CoreMessageWithTtlSchema zod intersection replaces type
ai.summary: CoreMessageWithTtlSchema defined via z.intersection(coreMessageSchema, ...). Replaces manual type intersection in common/src/types/message.ts. CoreMessageWithTtl type now inferred from schema. Covers Shared/Core types.

eli5.text: The assistant's message-format definition is now described in a single, consistent way instead of being patched together from scattered rules, which keeps how long messages stick around behaving the same as before. You, as someone using the assistant, won't notice any visual or functional difference today. Because the way messages are described internally is now unified, the code that manages how long saved messages last is simpler and less likely to break in future updates.

ai.title: AI SDK transformMessages extracts toolCallId from CoreToolMessage
ai.summary: The `transformMessages` function in `backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts` now handles tool messages by checking for `tool_call_id` directly or extracting `toolCallId` from the first part of `CoreToolMessage` content arrays. This fixes failures where tool messages lacked the direct `tool_call_id` property, previously causing undefined references or errors during transformation. The change is scoped to the backend AI SDK adapter, ensuring robust tool call ID resolution for both OpenAI-style and CoreToolMessage formats.

eli5.text: When the assistant talks to other AI services, it now reads tool call IDs correctly from two different message formats instead of only one. Previously, messages in the second format caused crashes because the ID was missing; now the assistant looks inside the message content to find it when the direct spot is empty. You won't see anything on your screen, but behind the scenes this stops those messages from failing and keeps things from breaking when handling tool results.

ai.title: Refactor: make system parameter optional in transformMessages
ai.summary: Updated `transformMessages` in `backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts` to make the `system` parameter optional (`system?: System`) instead of explicitly accepting `undefined`. This simplifies the type signature for callers not passing a system prompt. The change is internal to the Vercel AI SDK adapter.

eli5.text: The behind-the-scenes helper that converts incoming messages for the AI no longer requires a system instruction to be explicitly turned off; omitting it now works the same as turning it off before. Nothing you see changes today. This is purely a small internal cleanup within the AI messaging layer.

ai.title: Remove dedicated OpenAI API client in favor of unified Vercel AI SDK
ai.summary: Deleted `openai-api.ts` and replaced all `promptOpenAI` calls with `promptAiSdk` from `./vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk`. The refactor consolidates backend LLM routing through a single provider-agnostic module, eliminating the separate OpenAI client initialization and its Helicone proxy headers. Files affected: `fast-rewrite.ts`, `relace-api.ts`, `process-file-block.ts`, and the removed `openai-api.ts`.

eli5.text: The app now sends all its requests to language models through one single connection method instead of keeping a separate shortcut just for OpenAI. As a result, the code that talked directly to OpenAI and routed traffic through an analytics service called Helicone has been deleted entirely. Internal developers will notice the unified module is now the only way any backend request reaches a language model, and the extra OpenAI-only setup is gone.

ai.title: Replace direct Claude API with Vercel AI SDK in backend
ai.summary: Internal refactoring replaces direct Anthropic SDK calls in `backend/src/llm-apis/claude.ts` with the unified `promptAiSdk` interface from `backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts`. This change standardizes LLM interactions across admin tools and prompt generation scripts, removing custom retry logic and message transformation handling specific to the raw Claude API. The `ai-sdk.ts` module now supports `chargeUser` options and `TEST_USER_ID` for internal testing contexts, ensuring consistent billing and logging behavior for non-user-facing operations.

eli5.text: The admin tools that help manage and evaluate how well the assistant performs its tasks have been rewired to use a single, shared method for talking to the AI instead of one approach specifically for Claude. You won't see a difference in how anything works right now, but behind the scenes, grading runs, relabeling files, and generating diffs all now go through the same internal channel, which simplifies maintenance and ensures consistent billing and logging for these internal operations. Several older, duplicated ways of calling the AI have been removed.

ai.title: Add CoreMessageWithTtl type and transform logic
ai.summary: Added `CoreMessageWithTtl` type in `common/src/types/message.ts` extending `CoreMessage` with a `timeToLive` field. Updated `transformMessages` in `backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts` to accept this new type and pass it through to `CoreMessage[]` if present. This supports TTL-based message handling in the AI SDK integration layer.

eli5.text: A message can now be given a timeout that decides how long it sticks around before it gets cleared out. When the system processes incoming messages, any message carrying that timeout now skips the normal conversion step and goes straight through unchanged, while ordinary messages keep being translated as before. The change is in place in the code today and ready for the AI layer to start issuing or honoring those timeouts, but it only takes effect once something actually attaches one.

ai.title: Remove backend/src/llm-apis/deepseek-api.ts
ai.summary: Deleted `backend/src/llm-apis/deepseek-api.ts` (-264 lines). Removes the Deepseek API integration layer, including stream handling, timeout/retry logic, and image stripping. Scope: backend LLM APIs. Internal cleanup; no direct user-facing behavior change visible in this diff.

eli5.text: The team removed the code that let the system talk to the Deepseek model, which had been used to send requests, wait for answers with timeouts and retries, and quietly strip out image data (since Deepseek didn't support images yet). No one should notice anything different when they use the product right now, because this is behind-the-scenes cleanup; the feature still works the same way until they switch to a different way of calling Deepseek or another provider. If you opened the code folder, you'd find that one file gone and all its helper logic with it.

ai.title: Migrate promptFlashWithFallbacks to CoreMessage
ai.summary: Refactor `promptFlashWithFallbacks` in `backend/src/llm-apis/gemini-with-fallbacks.ts` to accept `CoreMessage[]` instead of `Message[]` and `System` arguments. Callers in `backend/src/fast-rewrite.ts`, `backend/src/tools.ts`, and file-finding utilities now wrap arguments with `transformMessages` before invoking the function. The fallback chain is simplified to route primary requests through `promptAiSdk` and remove direct Vertex/Gemini API handling.

eli5.text: The assistant's underlying language model helper function has been updated to use a more modern internal format for processing conversations. Instead of accepting messages in one specific layout, it now works with a newer, more flexible format that all callers already convert to before handing them off. The old direct connections to certain external AI services were removed, leaving a single, simplified path that routes requests through the preferred system. If you looked under the hood you'd see several files now pass their prepared message lists through a standard conversion step before sending them to the model, and one previously used interface file is no longer referenced.

eli5.text: You, as an internal tool consumer, won't see any difference when using the assistant's deep-thinking feature. The code that prepares your conversations for the thinking step was reorganized: instead of the thinking system doing that preparation itself, the system that calls it now does the prep work first and hands over ready-to-use messages. This is purely behind-the-scenes tidy-up with no change to how the feature behaves.

The check tool also creates the destination folder automatically if it doesn't exist yet. This only affects how the internal check reports are filed, not what the checks actually do.

ai.title: Add manifold eval set and runner
ai.summary: Added eval-manifold.json containing 941 lines of curated git commits from manifoldmarkets/manifold for regression testing. Introduced run-eval-set.ts to execute these specs against Freebuff, updating package.json with necessary dependencies. This expands internal evaluation coverage for complex prompt engineering and code generation tasks.

eli5.text: The system now has a new set of practice tests built from real past work done on Manifold Markets, letting the team automatically check that its AI-writing helper still behaves correctly as they tweak it. These tests are only used by the developers internally to catch problems before changes go live, so you won't notice anything different when using the assistant.

ai.title: Remove daily-git-evals GitHub Actions workflow
ai.summary: Deleted .github/workflows/daily-git-evals.yml. This workflow previously ran Codebuff git evaluations daily at 8am UTC to generate trace files. Scope limited to CI infrastructure; no user-facing code changes.

eli5.text: You wouldn't notice anything as a user, since this change only affects the internal scheduling tool the development team uses to run automated quality checks. That tool previously had a daily check-in that tested the assistant's coding help every morning, and that scheduled daily check has been removed. This is behind-the-scenes maintenance, so it doesn't change any features you use today.

ai.title: Add post-eval analysis to git eval runner
ai.summary: New `evals/post-eval-analysis.ts` implements LLM-driven analysis of `FullEvalLog` data, generating structured summaries, prioritized problems, and recommendations. `evals/run-eval-set.ts` now invokes `analyzeEvalResults` after each successful eval run, attaching the analysis to the result object. Type definition in `evals/git-evals/types.ts` updated to ensure `eval_runs` contains `EvalRunJudged` instances with `judging_results` required for analysis input. Analysis failures are caught and logged as warnings, allowing the eval pipeline to proceed without blocking on analysis errors.

eli5.text: After each automated test run of the assistant's responses, the system now automatically generates a written summary of what went well and what problems came up, including which issues are most important to fix first. This only affects the internal team who runs these test evaluations; you wouldn't see it in normal use. Behind the scenes, a new step reads the test results and writes up the findings, but if that step has a problem, it just logs a warning and lets the rest of the testing continue without stopping.

ai.title: evals pipeline sends results via Loops API
ai.summary: New `sendLoopsEmail` utility in `backend/src/util/loops.ts` posts transactional emails via Loops API. `evals/email-sender.ts` formats aggregated metrics and analysis into email content. `evals/run-eval-set.ts` triggers email dispatch after eval completion. `evals/post-eval-analysis.ts` exports `PostEvalAnalysis` type and schema for reuse.

eli5.text: Every time you run a set of evals, the system now writes up a quick human-readable summary and fires an email to whoever is configured to receive results, so you no longer have to dig through files to see how things went. The summary includes total runs attempted, how many succeeded, and the average scores for helpfulness, completion, and efficiency. To send the message it talks to an external email service, and it silently skips sending (with a warning) if the required API key hasn’t been set yet.

ai.title: Fix Loops email API dataVariables payload
ai.summary: Corrects the request body structure in `sendLoopsEmail` by wrapping `emailData` in a `dataVariables` object. This aligns the payload with the Loops API schema for transactional emails, ensuring custom data is correctly parsed. The change applies to `backend/src/util/loops.ts`.

eli5.text: Emails sent through our internal messaging system were arriving without their custom data filled in. The system was now fixed to send the extra information in the format the email service expects, so personalized details reach the right spots in the message. This runs behind the scenes and you wouldn't see anything change directly, but emails should render correctly now.

ai.title: Move post-eval analysis files to git-evals directory
ai.summary: Renamed evals/post-eval-analysis.ts and evals/email-sender.ts to evals/git-evals/. Updated imports in evals/run-eval-set.ts to reflect new paths. Extracted PostEvalAnalysis interface to shared module.

eli5.text: The team moved the files used to review test results and send summary emails into one shared folder, so they could be reused more easily later. The analysis report still appears in your terminal after a test run, showing the same top problems and frequency numbers. You wouldn't notice a change in what the report looks like or when it runs, but the developers have set up the shared interface so future analysis tools can plug into the same report format.

ai.title: Add /ask mode for read-only coding queries
ai.summary: New /ask cost mode enables read-only agent sessions, preventing file modifications and terminal command execution. Backend filters tools via getFilteredToolsInstructions and injects specific system prompts when costMode is 'ask'. Model routing assigns gemini-2_5_pro_preview for main prompts and claudeModels.haiku for fallbacks. Updates touch backend/src/tools.ts, common/src/constants.ts, and npm-app/src/cli.ts for command parsing and UI feedback.

eli5.text: When you ask the coding assistant a question, it can now enter a 'read-only' mode where it will not change any files or run terminal commands, letting you ask questions and get explanations without risk of automatic edits. The assistant is told it only has tools for answering questions, not for modifying your project. If you looked, you would see the assistant respond to queries with plans and explanations instead of making changes, and you would not see the dangerous tools (like file-writing or terminal commands) in its available actions during these sessions.

ai.title: CLI mode switch makes slash optional
ai.summary: The CLI regex in npm-app/src/cli.ts now makes the leading slash optional for cost mode commands. This allows users to type bare mode names (e.g., lite) instead of requiring the slash prefix (/lite). The change applies to lite, normal, max, experimental, and ask modes.

eli5.text: When using the command-line interface, you can now type mode names like "lite" or "normal" directly without needing to start with a slash. Previously, the system required a leading slash character before these words; now that slash is optional. This affects anyone typing commands into the CLI tool, making the input slightly more forgiving and quicker to type.

ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.299. Single change in npm-app/package.json.

eli5.text: You get version 1.0.299 by updating your installed copy; it quietly switches several backend services (like the OpenAI and Anthropic API clients) over to a single unified interface so future maintenance is easier, and the new read-only /ask mode is now usable if you choose it. Behind the scenes the system also drops its old Gemini integration and adds support for newer message formats that let AI conversations remember how long a message should stay around. For most users today nothing looks different yet unless you deliberately try the new /ask mode; the version number bump simply makes sure everyone who installs or updates now has this consolidated foundation.

ai.title: Add missing ai dependency to common package
ai.summary: Added `ai` version `^4.3.6` to `dependencies` in `common/package.json`. Fixes missing dependency error during build or runtime. Scope limited to shared core package configuration.

eli5.text: A shared set of tools used across the assistant's features was missing one of its own required building blocks, so the system could fail or stall when trying to assemble or run. That missing piece has now been added back in, allowing the shared tools to load and work properly wherever they are used. The fix is in effect now and happens behind the scenes; you would only notice if the assistant had been failing to start or build correctly before.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.300
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.300 in npm-app/package.json. Routine release increment.

eli5.text: Your copy of the assistant software has been updated to a new build number. If you use it, you'll get this fresh build automatically when you next install or update it. Inside this build, the assistant can now talk to a new AI model from Google, and it no longer sends your usage data to the old analytics address. Everything should work the same way for you.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.301
ai.summary: Version bumped from 1.0.300 to 1.0.301 in `npm-app/package.json`. Routine release increment.

eli5.text: A new version of the assistant was published, which bundles together several recent fixes: the analytics connection was switched back to its own direct address, a Gemini AI module was removed, and some behind-the-scenes code that handles messages was cleaned up and made more consistent. Nothing about how you use the assistant has changed, but installing the latest version will include these small corrections under the hood.

Anyone running a server, bot, or add-on built on top of the shared code will load a little less and take fractionally less time to boot. If you were to open the project folder today, the AI library simply would not be present where it used to sit, and one of the message-format definitions that relied on it has been switched to a placeholder, so that piece can no longer be checked for mistakes until it is restored.

ai.title: CI start-js crash detection switched to background PID check
ai.summary: Replaced timeout wrapper with background process launch and PID verification in ci.yml. Uses kill -0 to confirm process liveness after 0.5s sleep, killing and waiting on success. Scope limited to .github/workflows/ci.yml Test start-js script startup step. Avoids exit code 124 ambiguity by directly checking process state.

eli5.text: The system now checks whether the startup script is actually running instead of guessing based on a timer. A brief half-second pause gives a crashing process time to fail, and the system confirms the process is alive before cleaning it up. If the process dies during that window, the system reports a startup failure; if it survives, the system stops it and marks the test as passed. This makes a single internal build test more reliable today.

ai.title: Dead code expression in npm-app/src/index.ts
ai.summary: Adds a no-op expression `[''][1].split('')` to `npm-app/src/index.ts`. This appears to be leftover test or debug code, as it has no effect on the application logic. The change is isolated to the CLI entry point and does not affect other packages.

eli5.text: A stray line of leftover testing code was removed from the assistant's startup file. It does nothing today and changes nothing you would see, but it was cluttering the place where the assistant prepares to run. Nothing else in the assistant was touched.

ai.title: CI startup smoke test waits 10s and suppresses output
ai.summary: The CI startup check in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` now redirects `bun run start-js` output to `/dev/null` and increases the post-launch `sleep` from 0.5s to 10s. The original 0.5s window was too short for the process to initialize, risking false-positive crash detections. The termination step also switched from bare `kill` to `kill -TERM` to ensure graceful shutdown. Scope limited to the CI workflow; no user-facing surfaces affected.

eli5.text: When the build system runs its quick startup check, it now waits 10 seconds before deciding whether the app launched successfully. Previously, it only gave the app half a second to get going, which was too brief and could incorrectly flag a slow-but-healthy startup as a failure. The extra wait time makes that automated health check more reliable, so it won't falsely report problems with a process that simply needs a moment to boot up. This only affects the internal testing process that runs behind the scenes during development.

ai.title: Reset project file context cache on /reset
ai.summary: The CLI `/reset` command now clears the cached project file context before re-initialization. `initProjectFileContextWithWorker` in `npm-app/src/project-files.ts` accepts a `resetCache` flag that sets `cachedProjectFileContext` to undefined. This ensures fresh file indexing after session resets in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`.

eli5.text: When you run the /reset command to start a new session, the assistant now clears out any previously scanned files and starts fresh, rather than reusing old file context that might be outdated. This affects anyone who uses /reset during a project, ensuring that file visibility after a reset matches the current state of your project instead of whatever was known at the start of the prior session. If you looked, you'd notice this only in the small detail that freshly reset sessions reflect file changes made since the last reset, the code change is minor and lives behind the scenes in the session-reset logic.

ai.title: Add codesearch to TOOLSWHICHENDTHERESPONSE
ai.summary: Added `code_search` to the `TOOLS_WHICH_END_THE_RESPONSE` array in `backend/src/tools.ts`. This ensures the agent stops its response immediately after invoking the code search tool, preventing unnecessary continuation. The change affects backend tool execution logic.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to search code, it now stops right after it runs that search instead of keeping to talk. The system was already told to wrap up after using most other tools, but code search was missing from that list, so it would sometimes keep going. Now code search is treated the same way, and you'll notice the assistant no longer adds extra chat after finding the code you asked about.

ai.title: Log test user credits in message-cost-tracker
ai.summary: Added logging for test user credit usage in `message-cost-tracker.ts`. The `saveMessage` function now checks if `userId` matches `TEST_USER_ID`. If true, it logs cost details and returns early, skipping client notification and database insertion. This change removes the `TEST_USER_ID` check from `relace-api.ts`, centralizing test user handling in the cost tracker.

eli5.text: The system now keeps a private note of how many credits the special test account uses, instead of recording it like a regular account's activity. When a message comes from that test account, the system logs the cost details for review and skips the usual steps of notifying the user and saving the message to the database. This removes a duplicate check that was happening in another part of the software, so all handling of the test account now happens in one place. If you looked closely at the logs, you'd see new entries for test account usage where they didn't appear before.

ai.title: Remove truncation in eval results
ai.summary: Removed `.slice(0, 5)` and `.substring(0, 200)` truncation from problem lists and recommendations in `evals/git-evals/email-eval-results.ts` and `evals/run-eval-set.ts`. Full problem descriptions and all recommendations are now included in email summaries and console output. Scope limited to internal eval reporting utilities.

eli5.text: Emails and terminal output from the internal evaluation system now show the full list of problems and recommendations instead of cutting them short. Previously, only the top five problems and first eight recommendations appeared, with each problem description also trimmed to 200 characters. ai.title: UpdateFile handler reports full file content back to agent
ai.summary: The handleUpdateFile tool in npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts now appends the full lines.join('\n') to the success message for both created and modified files. This provides the agent with the complete post-change content, replacing the previous generic 'Wrote to file successfully' string. Scope is limited to the internal tool handler logic in the npm-app package. The change increases the payload size of the tool response by the entire file content length.

eli5.text: When the assistant saves a file for you, it now sends the full updated file contents back to itself in its response, instead of just a brief 'file saved' message. This affects only the internal file-handling logic used by the assistant, and the response now carries the entire file content rather than a short status note. If you were watching the assistant's internal communications, you would see longer, more detailed responses after every file save or edit, roughly the size of the file itself.
